documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28M for yearly exam.

Active: PSC (ursodiol), extensive UC in remission (mesalamine), pemphigus vulgaris (rituximab x2 spring 2023, prednisone taper), mild anemia.

Med reconciliation: prednisone still on our list from April. He finished the taper in the last week of September and has taken none since; removed today. Current: mesalamine 1.2 g x4 daily, ursodiol 300 mg TID. NKDA.

Interval: skin and mouth clear since summer. UC quiet, colonoscopy in August clean per GI letter. Dissertation work going well. Reserve drills monthly, annual training planned.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight back to 72.5. No oral erosions. Skin with a few faint pink macules on the chest, no blisters. Heart, lungs normal. Abdomen benign, no organomegaly.
PHQ-9: 2.

A/P:
- Pemphigus vulgaris, in remission off prednisone; derm follow-up in April.
- UC/PSC stable on mesalamine and ursodiol. CMP, CBC today.
- Anemia: CBC today.
- Lipids once more for baseline after a steroid course.
- Vaccines current for the season (flu/COVID 10/2023, PCV20 4/2023).
RTC 1 yr; labs again in June.

documents.title: Dermatology Follow-up
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology group. Visit 04/16/2024.

Pemphigus vulgaris, one year from diagnosis. Rituximab 1 g x 2 in April/May 2023; prednisone discontinued late September 2023. No oral or skin lesions since last summer.
Exam: oral mucosa intact. Trunk clear apart from faint residual dyspigmentation. Nikolsky negative.
Medications per patient: ursodiol, mesalamine. NKDA.

Assessment: complete remission off therapy.
Plan: no maintenance therapy at this point. Return at the first sign of mouth sores or blisters; we would consider retreatment then. Routine visit in one year or as needed.

documents.title: June labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Rowan, liver numbers unchanged, platelets normal, hemoglobin about 13, slightly under the normal line for men but better than last year. Nothing to do. See you in the winter.

events.reason: Surveillance colonoscopy, PSC with ulcerative colitis

reports.text: Segmental random colonic biopsies (cecum/ascending, transverse, descending/sigmoid, rectum): colonic mucosa with mild architectural chronicity, no active inflammation. Negative for dysplasia.
reports.conclusion: Quiescent colitis, all segments. No dysplasia.

documents.title: Surveillance Colonoscopy and PSC Review
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology and hepatology group. 08/20/2024.

Surveillance colonoscopy for PSC-associated pancolitis. Cecum reached, ileum intubated. Mucosa healed and featureless without erosions; no polyps or visible lesions. Random biopsies by segment: quiescent colitis, no dysplasia.
PSC: MRCP this summer unchanged from 2023, no dominant stricture or mass; CA 19-9 within normal limits.
Meds: mesalamine 4.8 g daily, ursodiol 300 mg three times daily. NKDA.
Plan: continue current therapy; colonoscopy and MRCP next summer.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Seen 04/03/2025.

Chief complaint: fever, cough and feeling unwell for 10 days.

HPI: 29-year-old man with primary sclerosing cholangitis on ursodiol, ulcerative colitis, and pemphigus vulgaris. Two weeks ago he came back from camping in the Mississippi River valley, where he went into caves and poked around old barns. Since then, steadily more tired, some weight loss, intermittent chest discomfort, fevers and a cough. No hemoptysis. No sick contacts. No known lung disease.
Meds: ursodiol 300 mg TID. Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother RA, maternal uncle UC.
Social: never smoker, alcohol 1-2 drinks a month because of his liver, grad student and Army Reservist.

Exam: febrile and tachycardic on arrival, nontoxic. Scattered ulcers in the mouth. Tender cervical lymph nodes. Diminished breath sounds with fine crackles at both bases. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, nontender.

Results: mild normocytic anemia. LDH 320, elevated. Chest x-ray with bilateral hilar adenopathy and patchy reticulonodular infiltrates.
Sputum collected for fungal culture.

MDM: subacute febrile illness with hilar adenopathy and nodular infiltrates after cave and barn exposure in an endemic area; endemic mycosis, most likely histoplasmosis, leads. Not hypoxic, tolerating oral intake. Discussed with infectious disease on call, who will see him in clinic within the week for antigen testing and treatment decision.

Disposition: discharged home. Acetaminophen for fever. Return for shortness of breath, chest pain, confusion or inability to keep fluids down. Follow up with PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED follow-up. Seen 4/3 for 10 days of fever, cough and malaise after a camping trip in the Mississippi River valley exploring caves and barns. CXR with bilateral hilar adenopathy and reticulonodular infiltrates, LDH elevated, Hb mildly low; sputum fungal culture pending. ED record received 4/4.

Today: still tired, cough a bit less, evening fevers to about 100. Eating OK. No dyspnea at rest.
Exam: vitals as charted. Mouth with a few small shallow ulcers. Small tender anterior cervical nodes. Fine crackles at both bases. Abdomen benign.

A/P: probable acute pulmonary histoplasmosis. Prior rituximab in 2023 lowers my threshold to treat. ID appointment confirmed for Wednesday 4/9. Will ask for the culture result to come here too. Return/ED for breathing trouble. Off drills until cleared.

medications.sig: Take 2 capsules (200 mg) by mouth three times daily for 3 days, then 2 capsules (200 mg) twice daily with food

documents.title: Infectious Disease Consultation
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Outside infectious disease clinic. Seen 04/09/2025.

Referred from the ED for fever, cough, hilar adenopathy and reticulonodular infiltrates after caving and barn exploration in the Mississippi River valley in mid-March. History of PSC on ursodiol, ulcerative colitis on mesalamine, and pemphigus vulgaris treated with rituximab in 2023 and prednisone through September 2023, now off therapy.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: tired, temp 37.9. Few shallow oral ulcers. Tender cervical nodes. Bibasilar fine crackles.

Data: ED chest film as described. Urine Histoplasma antigen sent today returned positive. Sputum fungal culture from the ED is in progress.

Assessment: acute pulmonary histoplasmosis, moderate, with prior B-cell depletion.
Plan:
1. Itraconazole 200 mg three times daily for 3 days, then 200 mg twice daily, planned 6 weeks total. Take with food; avoid acid suppressants.
2. Liver panel at baseline (today) and in two weeks given PSC; can be drawn at his PCP's office.
3. Follow up in 6 weeks with a repeat chest film.
4. Not fit for drills or field duty until cleared.

documents.title: Liver tests on itraconazole
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Rowan, liver panel two weeks into itraconazole is the same as your usual PSC numbers, no bilirubin rise. Copy sent to ID. How are the fevers?

documents.title: RE: Liver tests on itraconazole
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Gone since last weekend. Still a little cough. Energy coming back.

reports.text: PA and lateral. Hilar contours smaller than on 04/03/2025. Previously seen reticulonodular opacities have largely cleared. No effusion. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Improving bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and clearing infiltrates.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Outside infectious disease clinic. Visit 05/20/2025.

Acute pulmonary histoplasmosis, six weeks into itraconazole. Fevers ended in mid-April, cough gone, energy normal. Mouth ulcers healed. Liver tests on treatment were at his PSC baseline.
Sputum culture from the ED grew Histoplasma capsulatum.
Chest x-ray today: hilar nodes smaller, infiltrates mostly cleared.

Assessment: histoplasmosis, clinically resolved.
Plan: finish itraconazole tomorrow (5/21) and stop. No suppressive therapy. If he needs immunosuppression again, as with retreatment of pemphigus, please let us know first. He is cleared for duty from our standpoint; he mentions an upcoming deployment.

documents.title: Deploying soon
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ID cleared me and I finished the itraconazole. My unit is deploying at the end of the month and I'll be gone until around mid-September. Could you send 90-day refills of the mesalamine and ursodiol with extra, and a printout of my problem list and meds for the battalion surgeon?

documents.title: RE: Deploying soon
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Done: mesalamine and ursodiol sent as 90-day fills with a vacation override for a second fill. Summary letter with your problems, medications and specialists' contacts is in your documents tab. Stay safe and check in when you're home. If you get fevers, sores that won't heal, or bloody stools while away, get seen there.

documents.title: Vacation supply
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Called pharmacy re: early fills for deployment. Insurance override approved for mesalamine and ursodiol. Pt picking up tomorrow.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted this morning, worked in this afternoon.

HPI: home from a deployment in the Middle East in mid-September (months of patrols in remote desert, lots of insect bites, sleeping outdoors). About three weeks of fatigue, feeling feverish on and off, malaise that is getting worse, poor appetite, and weakness. Weight about the same. Also a sore on the right forearm from the deployment that has not healed with bandages and ointment. No cough, no diarrhea or blood, no new mouth sores or blisters. Took his meds throughout.

Exam: tired-looking. Vitals as charted. Anicteric. No oral lesions. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft; liver edge felt just below the costal margin and spleen tip palpable on inspiration. Right forearm: about 1.5 cm ulcer with raised, firm rolled border and clean base. No lymphangitic streaking.

A/P: subacute fever and malaise with hepatosplenomegaly and a chronic ulcer after desert deployment with heavy insect exposure. Worried about leishmaniasis, visceral and cutaneous; also relapse or dissemination of histoplasmosis, malaria, and other infection. Stat CBC with diff and CMP today. Will call tonight with results; likely needs admission for workup.

Addendum 18:45: WBC 1.8 with ANC 1.0, Hb 9.0, platelets 101; AST and ALT mildly above his baseline. Called patient. Spoke with the hospitalist at the regional hospital; direct admission to medicine tomorrow morning, bed confirmed for 8 am. ID notified. Told him to go to the ED tonight instead if fever climbs or he feels worse.

medications.sig: 210 mg (3 mg/kg) IV once daily on days 1-5, then on days 14 and 21

results.text: No growth at 5 days (2 of 2 sets)

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

reports.text: Skin, right forearm, edge of ulcer, 4 mm punch biopsy. Dermis with a dense mixed infiltrate rich in histiocytes. Giemsa stain highlights numerous small intracellular round to oval organisms within histiocytes. Fungal stain (GMS) negative. Addendum 10/10: Leishmania PCR performed on paraffin tissue is positive, Leishmania donovani complex.
reports.conclusion: Dermal histiocytic infiltrate with intracellular round and oval organisms on Giemsa; Leishmania PCR positive (L. donovani complex).

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, medicine service. Admitted 10/07/2025, discharged 10/12/2025. Received by fax after request.

Reason for admission: three weeks of fatigue, subjective fevers and worsening malaise, plus a forearm lesion that has not healed with local wound care; referred directly by PCP for pancytopenia.

History: 30-year-old man with PSC, ulcerative colitis, pemphigus vulgaris, and histoplasmosis treated in the spring. Returned recently from military service in the Middle East with months of patrols in remote desert terrain; frequent insect bites; no animal exposures and no freshwater swimming. Poor appetite and generalized weakness, no weight loss.
Home meds: ursodiol 300 mg TID, mesalamine 4.8 g daily. NKDA.

Exam on admission: tired, febrile to 38.3. Mild hepatosplenomegaly. Right forearm ulcer, 1.5 cm, with raised borders.

Key results: hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, WBC 2,200/mm3, platelets 85,000/mm3. Liver enzymes mildly elevated. Blood cultures negative. Rapid malaria antigen negative. Urine Histoplasma antigen negative. Forearm punch biopsy: intracellular round and oval organisms within histiocytes on Giemsa; Leishmania PCR positive, L. donovani complex.

Diagnosis: visceral leishmaniasis, with a cutaneous lesion at the right forearm.

Hospital course: ID consulted. Liposomal amphotericin B 3 mg/kg (210 mg) daily started 10/7, days 1 through 5 given inpatient with saline loading. Creatinine and potassium stayed normal. Fevers broke on day 3. Counts stable to slightly improved at discharge.

Discharge plan: remaining doses on day 14 (10/20) and day 21 (10/27) at the hospital outpatient infusion center. Continue home medications. CBC and BMP with each infusion. ID clinic in about 6 weeks, with monitoring for relapse over the next 6 to 12 months. PCP follow-up within a week. Return for fever, bleeding or bruising.

documents.title: Update from the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got admitted yesterday as planned. They biopsied the arm sore and started IV amphotericin. ID thinks it's leishmaniasis, waiting on more tests. Feeling a little better today.

documents.title: RE: Update from the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for keeping me posted. I'll follow along with the team. Book a visit with me within a week of discharge.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after admission 10/7-10/12 at the regional hospital. Discharge summary not yet received; history from patient, his discharge paperwork, and the ID team by phone.

Dx: visceral leishmaniasis (forearm biopsy with intracellular organisms on Giemsa, Leishmania PCR positive). Liposomal amphotericin B days 1-5 done inpatient; days 14 and 21 scheduled 10/20 and 10/27.

Since home: no fevers for a week. Appetite returning. Still tires easily. No bleeding or bruising. Forearm ulcer smaller.
Meds: ursodiol 300 mg TID, mesalamine 4.8 g daily, liposomal amphotericin B per ID. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Spleen tip still palpable. Right forearm ulcer about 1 cm, clean, border flatter.

A/P:
- Visceral leishmaniasis on treatment. CBC and BMP today (amphotericin). ID follow-up in December.
- PSC/UC: continue ursodiol and mesalamine; UC quiet.
- Anemia: worse with VL; follow counts.
- Flu and COVID vaccines after the amphotericin course.
Will request discharge summary.

documents.title: Last infusion
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Last amphotericin dose went in yesterday, day 21. Labs they drew were fine per the infusion nurse. Feeling much more like myself.

documents.title: RE: Last infusion
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great. Nurse visit next week for flu and COVID shots. I'll see the ID letter in December.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Discharge summary for 10/7-10/12 admission still not received. Called hospital HIM, faxed request. Told 5-7 business days.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Afebrile today. Flu vaccine L arm, 2025-26 COVID vaccine R arm. Tolerated well.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Outside infectious disease clinic. Visit 12/09/2025.

Visceral leishmaniasis (L. donovani complex) treated with liposomal amphotericin B 3 mg/kg on days 1-5, 14 and 21, completed 10/27. Feels well, eating normally, no fevers.
Exam: spleen not palpable; liver edge not felt. Right forearm: healed, flat hypopigmented scar.
Labs: hemoglobin 11.8, WBC 4.1, platelets 176. Renal function normal. Transaminases back to his PSC baseline.

Assessment: good early response.
Plan: CBC in four months and see him then to finish relapse surveillance. Return for fever, weight loss or cytopenias.
